text:
mina: quick heads-up — our A/B canary (group B = kernel-selection change from PR #4521) is showing a p50 regression ~15% and p95 tail growth on long-seq workloads. saw it first at 11:03 UTC in cluster-west.

raj: ouch. which metric Dash? tokens/sec or latency?

mina: latency. tokens/sec is fine for short seqs. p50 increased from 64ms -> 74ms on 2k seqs, p95 spiked ~30% on a subset of requests.

jules: do we have a flame/profile? can we get perf top or jemalloc stack?

mina: attached quick perf dump from canary node (trimmed):
```
Samples: 10000 of event 'cpu'
  28.3% kernel_selector.cpp:142 choose_kernel
  12.7% batching.cpp:87 try_merge_batch
  9.1% kv_cache.cpp:203 on_cache_miss
  6.4% aten::matmul
  5.0% gpu_scheduler.cpp:58 schedule_chunk
```

mina: note the kernel_selector spike only in group B. group A stays at ~11% there.

dave: that lines up with my local repro — when kernel hinting chooses the new fused attention kernel we see more conditionals that serialize parts of the batch. Might be a batching heuristic mismatch.

raj: could also be KV cache churn. the sample shows on_cache_miss at 9% — maybe cache TTL behavior for long sequences changed with the new kernel (different key layout?).

mina: agree. I added a small ci perf run: job/ci-perf-nightly reported p95 +28% after merging #4521. ci-bot: Perf CI failed on main — p95 increased by 28% (regression threshold 10%).

ci-bot: Job link: https://ci.internal/rdw/perf/4521-nightly (failing test: large_context_throughput)

jules: we should pause the canary rollout and start a bisect on the PR. @sre-ops can you hold traffic?

sre-ops: pausing canary B now. traffic diverted to group A. rolling back B->A ratio to 0% for that rollout. :white_check_mark:

dave: I'll run a git-bisect between the kernel-selector commits and instrument additional KV key prints to confirm key layout.

mina: thanks. low friction rollback done. can we also add an automatic SLO gate so future A/B rollouts rollback automatically if p95 regresses >12% for 10m?

raj: we have the rollout controller but no auto-slo action for perf yet. we can add a simple guard: monitor per-route p95 per-canary-group, if breach -> pause and notify. I can prototype today.

jules: make sure it looks at stable baseline (group A) and not global aggregate. false positives if group A noisy.

dave: local bisect point: suspect commit 7f3a8 -> added fused-attn fallback logic and changed kernel priority table. reproducing now.

mina: for the postmortem/notes: include flame, KV key sample, and the canary gating timeline (pause at 11:10, rollback at 11:12).

sre-ops: logged incident ID INF-2026-0042 and pinned the canary pause in rollout console.

raj: after bisect we should add a unit test that runs kernel selection + synthetic batch shapes to catch serialization patterns. small e2e perf test in CI.

mina: agreed. thanks everyone — will post a follow-up with bisect result and the profile diff.

dave: quick note: if fused kernel is the culprit, we might be able to keep it but adjust batching heuristic to avoid combining small and long sequences in same batch. less risky than full revert.

jules: good plan. once bisect confirms, we can land a guarded rollout: kernel change + batching tweak + SLO gate.

mina: closing loop — rollback confirmed, canary paused, investigation in progress.
